packageRules.description: Group RustCrypto digest-ecosystem crates so they upgrade in lockstep. The `digest` trait crate is shared by sha*, hmac, rsa, signature, etc., and a major bump of one (e.g. sha1 0.10 -> 0.11 moves to digest 0.11) breaks compilation against any sibling still on the old `digest` major. Keeping them in one PR forces them to land together.

Group webrtc with its sans-io core rtc so they upgrade in lockstep. webrtc pins rtc to an exact patch and exposes rtc types (Packet, RtpCodecKind, RTCRtpCodecParameters) in its public API, so bumping either alone puts two rtc versions in the graph and shakenfist-spice-webrtc fails to compile (see #393 / #394).

Group openh264 with openh264-sys2 so they upgrade in lockstep. shakenfist-spice-compression pins both exactly: its H.264 encoder sets options through openh264-sys2's raw types that openh264 does not re-export, so the pair must be the one openh264 was released with, and bumping either alone either fails to resolve or puts two openh264-sys2 builds in the graph.

Group every IronRDP crate so they upgrade in lockstep with ironrdp-server. shakenfist-spice-rdp depends directly on crates whose types ironrdp-server takes but does not re-export (cliprdr, core, pdu, svc, rdpsnd, displaycontrol), at the versions ironrdp-server builds on, and the connector side shares picky, which ironrdp-connector pins exactly. Bumping any one alone either puts two versions of a trait crate in the graph and fails to compile, or fails to resolve. The group PR can only land once an ironrdp-server release has moved to the new versions, so the group is held for dependency dashboard approval rather than opened automatically: an ironrdp-* release almost always lands before the matching ironrdp-server one, and the resulting PR then sits red and burns a CI run on every push until upstream catches up (see #668 / #669 / #676 / #687). Tick the ironrdp entry on the dependency dashboard once ironrdp-server has a release that builds on the new ironrdp-connector.

Hold sha1 < 0.11 until rsa 0.10 stable releases. sha1 0.11 moves to digest 0.11, but our transitive rsa 0.9 still requires digest 0.10, so Sha1 no longer satisfies rsa::Oaep::new's DynDigest bound. Tracked in shakenfist/ryll#93 / RustCrypto/RSA#647.
Hold rand < 0.9 until rsa 0.10 stable releases. rand 0.9 restructured CryptoRngCore, which rsa 0.9 calls through. Tracked in shakenfist/ryll#93 / RustCrypto/RSA#647.
Hold rand_core < 0.10 to stay aligned with the rand 0.8 / rsa 0.9 pin above. Tracked in shakenfist/ryll#93 / RustCrypto/RSA#647.
